briefing.opening: Good morning/afternoon. Welcome to the climate briefing for August 16, 2026. Today, both globally and domestically, the harsh reality of climate change-induced disasters has once again been laid bare, while various efforts and policy discussions to counter them have continued.

sections.title: 🔴 Global Climate Crisis Spreading and Intensifying
sections.content: This summer, the harsh reality of climate change has globally struck the European economy [22, 26], with major European rivers turning into sandbanks filled with shipwrecks, and the Danube River devastated by drought, revealing 'hunger stones' and causing difficulties in securing drinking water [23, 33]. Across Europe, record-breaking heatwaves are accompanied by raging wildfires, and the UK is experiencing its hottest summer on record [35]. In Canada's Okanagan region, drought and wildfires caused by climate change continue to inflict damage [25].

sections.title: 🇰🇷 Domestic Climate Disaster Response and Vulnerability
sections.content: Domestic southern regions have experienced a triple threat of heavy rainfall and heatwaves following a drought, exposing gaps in disaster response [6]. Notably, during the Liberation Day holiday, a 'water bomb' of over 200mm poured down overnight in the southern regions, with Haenam recording 201mm of precipitation, and Mokpo breaking its highest hourly rainfall record for August, leading to widespread damage from flooded homes and roads [13]. In the Jeju region, the triple threat of heatwaves, cold waves, and droughts is shaking the survival foundations of the elderly population [5], and the need for changes in rice farming methods in the era of climate change has been raised [1].

sections.title: 🌱 Climate Action and Technological Innovation Efforts
sections.content: Positive movements for change have also been observed. Cheongdo-eup implemented climate change education programs at senior welfare centers [2], and Seongdong-gu proactively supported vulnerable households in preparation for heatwaves, showing positive results [3]. 'Our Neighborhood Circular Hubs,' where residents participate in achieving carbon neutrality, are expanding [7], and Sacheon City also promoted a carbon-neutral lifestyle practice campaign for 'Blue Sky Day' [8]. In the technology sector, Youngin ST announced an AI-MRV-based integrated platform for ESG response, carbon neutrality, and environmental analysis [9], and ESS (Energy Storage Systems) are emerging as a solution to power shortages in the AI era, becoming a new growth axis for renewable energy expansion [12].

sections.title: ⚠️ Energy Policy and Economic Challenges
sections.content: Challenges and policy discussions in the energy transition process are also active. While wind and solar power generation may appear inexpensive, concerns have been raised that actual generation costs increase when system costs are factored in [10]. Domestically, there are concerns that the Yoon Suk-yeol administration's shift from the Moon Jae-in administration's renewable energy expansion policy stance could hinder industrial growth [11]. There is a growing recognition that the climate crisis is closely linked to food, soil, and land [15], and an analysis has suggested that backlash against climate action could actually be a sign of net-zero progress [32].

sections.title: 🌍 Climate Crisis Awareness and International Discussions
sections.content: The international community is focusing on raising awareness of the climate crisis and exploring response measures. In Bangladesh, a workshop on reporting climate change loss and damage was held for journalists [21], and the REDD+ initiative aims to restore degraded land and enhance climate resilience [27]. An exclusive interview with Simon Stiell, Executive Secretary of the UN Climate Change Convention, shed light on the current state of international discussions [31], and new questions are being raised about which trees will survive in the era of climate crisis, alongside research on how climate change combines with 'super El Niño' [16, 24].

briefing.closing: Today's briefing has once again reminded us that climate change is no longer a problem of the future, but an ongoing catastrophe. At the same time, we have seen that global and domestic efforts and technological innovations to combat this crisis are continuously being sought. This concludes today's climate briefing.
